# Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop — facts

> Source-anchored units about Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop: 13 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 13 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Index creation uses memory and temporary disk files when its memory allowance is exhausted. Percona identifies rebuilding large collections or rebuilding with insufficient available memory as expensive. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/new-in-mongodb-4-4-hidden-index/
- [statement] Modern optimized builds briefly lock the collection at the start and end while yielding to reads and writes in between; the older Studio 3T description of database-wide foreground blocking throughout a build should not be applied to this process. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/mongodb-index-strategy/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Recreating a dropped unique index can fail if duplicate keys exist at completion, including duplicates written during the build; recovery may require data cleanup or write controls. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/README.md
- [statement] Cost-governance inference: evaluate index-removal savings alongside workload-specific rebuild time and resource contention. These sources support a recovery-risk assessment, but do not establish a fixed Atlas rebuild fee or a general dollar estimate. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/new-in-mongodb-4-4-hidden-index/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Hiding a candidate index before dropping it permits a query-performance trial and avoids rebuilding if the index is needed; Atlas documentation says unhiding takes less time than rebuilding a dropped index. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/new-in-mongodb-4-4-hidden-index/, https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/mongodb-index-strategy/, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-816
- [statement] A conventional index rebuild scans collection documents, generates and sorts index keys, and loads the resulting index. It uses memory and can spill temporary build data to disk; restoring an index definition alone does not restore the built index. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/index_builds/README.md
- [statement] Building an index competes for CPU and I/O resources. On a write-heavy collection, an index build can reduce write performance and take longer, so recovery planning must account for production load. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/how-to-perform-rolling-index-builds-with-percona-operator-for-mongodb/
- [statement] A hidden index still receives write updates and consumes storage and memory. Hiding is a trial of query-planner impact, not realization of the storage and maintenance savings expected from dropping the index. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/mongodb-index-strategy/, https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/DRIVERS-816, https://www.percona.com/blog/new-in-mongodb-4-4-hidden-index/
- [statement] Hiding a unique index preserves its uniqueness constraint, and hiding a TTL index preserves document expiry. A hide trial therefore does not simulate removal of these index functions. (medium confidence) — https://studio3t.com/knowledge-base/3t-build/desktop-ide/mongodb-index-strategy/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/new-in-mongodb-4-4-hidden-index/
- [statement] Optimized MongoDB index builds hold an exclusive collection lock at the beginning and end, while allowing interleaved reads and writes during the main build. Allowing concurrent traffic does not eliminate build resource consumption or performance impact. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/how-to-perform-rolling-index-builds-with-percona-operator-for-mongodb/
- [statement] For a showback decision, treat rebuild resource use and degraded application performance as possible offsets to recurring savings from a drop. This is a cost-accounting inference from the documented mechanisms, not a measured financial outcome or a fixed rebuild price. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/drop-indexes.md · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.percona.com/blog/how-to-perform-rolling-index-builds-with-percona-operator-for-mongodb/
- [statement] Heavy writes during an index build can reduce write performance and lengthen the build; MongoDB recommends considering a window that reduces or stops writes. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop
- [statement] Replicated index builds run across data-bearing replica-set members and require a commit quorum. With the documented votingMembers quorum, an unreachable voting data-bearing member can stall completion. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: Index rebuild cost after a wrong drop
